label: early original-phase k/z/3 (also r/h/m) input following a z/k/3/r/l/o/m/2 token
predicate: (phase == 0) & (t >= 1) & (t <= 4) & isin(in_tok, [tok("k"), tok("z"), tok("3"), tok("r"), tok("h"), tok("m")]) & isin(prev_tok, [tok("z"), tok("k"), tok("3"), tok("r"), tok("l"), tok("o"), tok("m"), tok("2")])
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase, at early positions t=1..5 (83% of mass at t=2-3), never at t=0, the delimiter, or the copy phase. Strongly token-selective on the current input: k (8x lift), z, 3 (5-7x), then r, h, m (2-3x); other tokens rarely. Also depends on preceding context: activation is much more likely when the previous token (and earlier tokens / first token) come from a similar set {z,k,3,r,l,o,m,2}, so it looks like a graded sum of token-specific contributions over the first few inputs, not a clean boolean. The largest activations are runs like z k k / z z z / k z k at t=2-3. The in_tok AND prev_tok predicate gets dev F1 0.49 (P 0.40, R 0.64, mass recall 0.77). Precision stays low because many k/z/3 inputs with a matching previous token still do not cross the threshold. Using the whole prefix (n_seen) did not help beyond ~0.50.
